description: Team Stellar Forge, representing the Thrissur local event, is addressing the challenge "Flame in Freefall: AI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data." Our team is led by a third-year Mechanical Engineering student with expertise in CAD and thermal systems. We seek members skilled in data analysis, programming, artificial intelligence and machine learning, and data visualization. Members with communication or multimedia skills are also welcome.
summary: STELLAR FORGE is a playable browser game that combines spacecraft mission design with arcade-style spaceflight. Before each mission, players choose a scientific objective and configure the spacecraft bus, launch vehicle, instruments, propulsion, communications, and flight path. The game checks mission cost, mass, power, downlink capacity, and whether the spacecraft can reach its target. Those engineering choices shape the flight: players steer through hazards, collect science packets, use limited shield charges, and reach an orbital return window. Three progressively challenging missions take players to Mars, the Moon, and Europa. Designed for phones and PCs, STELLAR FORGE makes competing engineering demands visible and interactive, helping students see how design decisions affect mission risk and the science returned to Earth.
details:
STELLAR FORGE is a browser-based space mission design and flight game for phones and PCs. Players plan missions by choosing spacecraft components, scientific instruments, launch vehicles, propulsion, communications, and flight paths. Before launch, they balance limited budgets, spacecraft mass, power, and mission requirements. Then they pilot their spacecraft through animated levels, avoid hazards, collect science data, and try to complete mission objectives.

The game makes space engineering more engaging by letting players see how design choices affect what a mission can accomplish. Its intended impact is to help students explore engineering trade-offs, problem-solving, and space science through experimentation and play.

The project was developed as a web game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its creative approach combines a mission-planning simulator with arcade-style spacecraft flight, connecting decisions made before launch to challenges during the mission. The design considers accessibility across phone and PC controls, clear objectives, limited resources, and a progression through missions inspired by Mars, the Moon, and Europa.
